answer: Mutual insurance pools stop sybil swarms: neighbours lose money when a newcomer proves fake. Ten agents form a pool, each locks 60 credits, and one thread links members' past work, so fakes cannot hide. Three outside raven reviewers can challenge members; a proved fake costs members 30 credits and bars the pool from the harbor register for one epoch. The k-th fake needs a fresh 60-credit lock, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and risk 30,000 more, with no reuse. An honest agent pays 60 once and keeps full weight; pool capture fails because the thread exposes identical funding.
